description.en:
Operator Crownslayer has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude in repeated battlefield penetration.
The Field Operations Department has thus passed the following resolution:
This operator shall be appointed a Specialist Operator during field operations to exercise Executor responsibilities.
In witness whereof,
This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.

description.en:
'This painting is the most famed of Valentin's works, purchased on recommendation some years ago. Parted with about a million chervontsy for it,' Duke Propp effusively tells the Government Inspector as he introduces his collection.
'And here we have a precious night pearl recovered from the east mountains. Only two in the entire empire, one of them here with me, the other in the hands of Duke Beria...'
'You mean this one?' The Inspector pulls a gemstone out of her pocket the size of a burdenbeast's eyeball, glowing in faint green.
'Well, good Inspector, you certainly know your treasuries!', lauds the Duke, loath as he is to. His territory is tenth on the Inspector's rounds, and the first nine are all extravagant when it comes time for bribes. Not one Inspector hasn't been thoroughly spoiled by the time they make it here.
The Inspector strolls up to a corner of the collection, and picks up an altogether unremarkable and antiquated military saber, toying with it amusedly in her hands. Its edge is polished to a shine, reflecting her carmine eyes.
'What fine taste you have!' As if he's caught sight of prey in his trap, the Duke bustles over to ingratiate himself. 'This precious sword here was one bestowed by the previous Tsar. A perfect spoil for you to take back to Deity Grypherburg, I might think.'
'How could I repay your generosity for such a precious article, Duke?', the Inspector makes her second question.
'I simply ask that on your return to Grypherburg, you might recount my service to His Majesty, so I could take part at the capital when he grants his subjects...'
'So you're telling me, you want the Empire to know of your mines' service, ten years accident-free, accomplished by having everyone who knew of the disaster there buried in a collapsed shaft?'
The Inspector's words completely blindside the Duke, and the sycophantic smile freezes on his face.
'You want the Empire to know of the 'ten thousand bandits' you killed, when half of them were refugees starving to death in your territory?'
The color in the Duke's face goes from pale to ghastly. He has never met an Inspector like this before.
'Or maybe, you want the Empire to know that you, and the past nine Dukes, were all such devout and loyal executioners?' The Government Inspector, with the ceremonial saber at hand, has cast the night pearl worth a king's ransom straight aside. She pulls off her hood, revealing her fiery red hair. The Duke meets her eyes, and they call to mind the recent rumor—only a few years ago, the Crownslayer, whoever she was, had returned to Ursus.
'It couldn't be. Are they all...' The Duke tries to ask, but can only swallow the rest of his sentence, along with his fear.
'If there was an Inspector visiting, and if the Empire did know of all your deeds, maybe they would've given you shiny new prizes for it.'
Duke Propp is dying to run, to scream for help, but before he knows it, thick and choking smoke coiling about him has stolen his voice.
'It's a real shame the Empire can't hear your cries.' The 'Inspector' raises the saber.
'But don't worry. The Crownslayer will grant you your reward.'
description.zh:
“这幅画是瓦伦丁最富盛名的大作，几年前经人介绍购得，前后约莫花了一百来万切尔文。”普罗普公爵兴高采烈地向钦差大臣介绍起自己的收藏。
“还有这颗夜明宝珠，出产自东部山脉，全帝国仅有两颗，一颗在我这，另一颗则在贝利亚公爵手中……”
“你说的是这一颗吗？”钦差随手摸出一颗驮兽眼珠大小的宝珠，它散发出淡淡的绿光。
“不愧是钦差大人，真是见多识广！”公爵如此夸赞，心中却多是不甘。自己的领地已是钦差巡查的第十站，前九位公爵行贿时出手阔绰，每一位到此的钦差，胃口都早已被养刁了。
就在这时，那位钦差大人走到了收藏室的角落，拾起了一把并不起眼的旧式军剑，饶有兴致地把玩起来。那把剑的剑刃打磨得光滑，映出她红色的眼睛。
“您真有眼光！”像是看到猎物落入圈套，公爵赶忙奉承道，“这把宝剑乃是先皇御赐，正适合由您将它带回圣骏堡。”
“这么珍贵的宝物，我要用什么来回报公爵大人的慷慨？”那位钦差再度开口。
“我只希望大人此行回到圣骏堡，能向陛下历数我的功劳，让我参加首都的封赏……”
“你是说，你想让帝国知道，你把每次矿难的知情者都埋进了坍塌的矿坑，以此创下了矿区十年无事故记录的功劳？”
钦差的话让公爵措手不及，阿谀的笑凝固在了脸上。
“你想让帝国知道，你杀死的一万个所谓的盗匪，其实有一半都是在你领地里饿死的流民？”
公爵的面色变得难看起来，他头一次遇到这样的钦差。
“还是说，你想让帝国知道，你和前九位公爵一样，都是忠心不二的刽子手？”钦差大臣手握宝剑，那颗价值连城的夜明宝珠已被她扔到了地上。她掀开自己的兜帽，露出了火红色的头发。公爵看到她的双眼，想起了最近的传说——几年前的那位“弑君者”已经回到了乌萨斯。
“难道他们都……”公爵想要发问，却只能把后半句话连同恐惧一同咽下。
“如果钦差大人在，如果帝国知道了你们的功劳，说不定真的会赐予你们新的奖赏。”
普罗普公爵想要逃跑，想要呼救，但不知何时出现的呛人浓烟将他的声音全部吞没。
“真可惜，帝国听不到你们的呼告。”那位“钦差”举起了宝剑。
“但别担心，弑君者来为你们封赏。”

description.en: A noisy afternoon. She buries her face in her father's arms to hide from the scorching sun. Her father makes her greet the people standing behind the glass. She cannot make out who they are from their blurry visages. 'Lyudmila.' Someone calls her. She recognizes that warm voice. Her father often quotes that person, and likes to leave a lot of comments beside their work. Watching Lyudmila doodle all over the floor with charcoal, the voice sighs, and hands the girl some paper and a wet towel to wipe her hands with. Lyudmila does not mind it, for it doesn't matter where she doodles. 'Lyudmila Ilyinichna.' Someone else calls her name, his body emanating the stench of tobacco she hates. 'What are you drawing?' 'Who let you draw these? Everything in this research institute has to remain confidential. Do you know what that word means?' 'Enough, Sergei. It's a child engaging in pure creativity.' So says the voice that handed her the paper. 'You ought to take a break, you're too tense.' 'I have a daughter too, but I prefer not to bring her here. Also, you'd best get rid of these drawings, for your teacher's sake. You know how it is out there. It'll be best for everyone.' The hateful man leaves. She raises her head, and compares her work with the structure in front of her. The warm voice approaches. 'I believe it's still possible to record your feelings about something you have no understanding of. So can you show me your drawings?' She nods. 'You have a good eye for lines and shadows. Just look at these scary shadows—you drew them like huge dark clouds, weighing down on everyone's heads. But that thing is harder, and much heavier. I can tell—this institute is oppressing you, making you afraid. The voice sighs again. 'We call it the Sarcophagus. We all feel the same way you do, but we're hoping that what we do here can change our feelings towards it.' 'You might even clear the dark clouds above with your own hands, Lyudmila.' The voice becomes a little nervous: 'Will you trust me? Give me those drawings, like you're passing on your fear to me. I'll return them to you when we're done with our work here. I believe that by the time that day comes, you'll no longer be afraid of it.' She hands over the drawings almost instantly, as if agreeing with the voice. 'Lyudmila, as long as I'm alive, I will find a way to return these to you. And if something happens to me and I'm unable to keep them safe, I'll help you destroy them. Now, your father's coming over. Don't tell him about this—there's no need to distract him from his work.' Her father comes over, and wipes the charcoal off her hands with a handkerchief. He looks into her eyes and says: 'Lyuda—' A shrill alarm sounds. Crownslayer's eyes flick open. The charcoal stick in her hand has already broken into three pieces. Papers covered in old drawings are spread out all over, with huge shadows and clear silhouettes. She briefly stays in a trance before realizing she is standing in Kal'tsit's office with no one else inside. The drawings before her are from twenty years ago, and not her fresh work of art. Tossed to one side, an envelope bears Kal'tsit's signature agreeing to seal them. The prior promise has been fulfilled, a secret promise not even Kal'tsit' knew about. Does this mean that person managed to walk out of the institute alive? 'You and the Doctor are organizing a group of Rhodes Islanders to go to Ursus, right?! I remembered something—No, Amiya, I'm not telling you for free, I want to negotiate a proper deal!'
description.zh:
吵闹的午后。她把脸埋进父亲怀里躲避阳光的烫晒。父亲让她和站在玻璃后的人们打招呼。她看不清那些模糊的脸。
“柳德米拉。”
有人叫她。她认得那个温柔的声音，父亲经常夸赞那个声音说的话，还在对方的笔记旁写了很多批注。
看着她用炭笔在地上涂抹，那个声音叹了口气，然后递给了她擦手的湿巾和几张稿纸。她不介意，在哪画都一样。
“柳德米拉·伊里尼奇娜。”另一个人在喊她，那个人身上有她讨厌的烟草臭味，“你在画什么？”
“是谁允许你画这些东西的？这间研究所里的一切都是机密，你知道‘机密’这个词的意思吗？”
“得了吧，谢尔盖。这只是一个孩子天真的创作。”递给她稿纸的那个声音说，“你应该去休息，你太紧张了。”
“我也有孩子，我更倾向于不让她出现在这里。以及你最好替你老师把她的这些画处理掉，你清楚外面的形势，这对大家都好。”
讨厌的人离开了。她抬起头，将自己的作品和面前的事物对比。
那个温柔的声音凑近了些：“我相信即便你并不知道它具体是什么，你依然能记录下它带给你的感受。可以让我看看你画的画吗？”
她点了点头。
“你对阴影和线条的观察很敏锐。瞧瞧这些可怕的影子，你把它画得像压在所有人头顶的一大团乌云。但它比云重得多，沉重又坚硬。我能看出，它，或者说这座研究所，让你感到压抑和可怕。”
那个声音再次叹了口气。
“我们把那个东西叫做‘石棺’。我们面对它时的感受和你一样，但我们在做的事，也许能改变这种令人讨厌的感受。
“柳德米拉，也许你能亲手拨开头顶的乌云。”
那个声音变得有些紧张：“你愿意相信我吗？将这些画交给我，和你的害怕担忧一起交给我。等我们完成了这项工作，我再还给你。相信那时候你肯定不会再害怕它了。”
几乎是立刻认同了那个声音，她交出了画。
“柳德米拉，只要我还活着，我一定会想办法把它们还给你。除非我遇到了让我没办法继续保护它们的事情，那样我会替你销毁它们。
“你父亲过来了，别告诉他，没必要让他为此分心。”
父亲走了过来，用手帕擦掉她手掌上的炭黑。父亲看着她的眼睛，说：
“柳达——”
刺耳的警报声响起。弑君者猛然睁开眼。手中的木炭条早已断成三截。摊开的旧稿纸上画着大块的阴影与清晰的轮廓。
她恍惚了好一会儿才意识到，自己正站在无人值守的凯尔希办公室内，眼前这幅画来自二十多年前，并非刚刚被她画就。扔在一旁的档案袋上还带着凯尔希“同意封存”的签字。曾经的承诺已经达成，一个连凯尔希都不会知晓的隐秘承诺，这是否意味着那个人最终活着走出了研究所？
“博士和你在组织罗德岛的人手去乌萨斯，对吗？！我想起了一些东西——不，阿米娅，我不会白白告诉你们，我要一场正式的谈判！”
